note: context_advanced_datalayer adds one Context reaction (@ContextReaction id=context_advanced_datalayer) that lets you set Advanced Datalayer tag values inside a Context, so datalayer variables can be applied conditionally (path/role/entity). Values are stored at context.context.<name>.reactions.context_advanced_datalayer as a tag_id => value map. hook_advanced_datalayer_alter() merges every ACTIVE reaction's values into the datalayer before it is pushed (via context.manager->getActiveReactions). Depends on context + advanced_datalayer; no routes/permissions/services/config schema of its own. Medium cases create a Context with the reaction carrying a known tag value and read it back; hard cases build a Context with the reaction, verified against the context config entity. Tag ids come from advanced_datalayer tag plugins (example_advanced_datalayer is enabled, providing site_Name, event, etc.).

evals.prompt: What does the context_advanced_datalayer submodule add on top of Advanced Datalayer, and what does it let a site builder do that the base module's per-page-type defaults do not?
evals.expected_output: It adds a Context reaction (context_advanced_datalayer) so you can set dataLayer tag values inside a Context and apply them conditionally (by path, role, entity type, etc.), rather than only per page type.

evals.prompt: Which two Drupal modules must be enabled for context_advanced_datalayer to work?
evals.expected_output: It depends on both context and advanced_datalayer (and you need datalayer tags to exist, e.g. from example_advanced_datalayer or your own tag plugins).

evals.prompt: How do the tag values configured in a context_advanced_datalayer Context reaction actually end up in the page's dataLayer?
evals.expected_output: Via hook_advanced_datalayer_alter(): the module asks context.manager->getActiveReactions('context_advanced_datalayer') for all currently-active reactions, executes each, and merges their tag_id => value maps into the datalayer array before it is pushed.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a Context named cadl_eval that uses the Advanced Datalayer context reaction. Inspect its live configuration and report the value it sets for the site_Name dataLayer tag.
On this Drupal site, the Context cadl_eval uses the Advanced Datalayer context reaction to set an 'event' dataLayer value. Inspect the live configuration and report the event value it sets.

On this Drupal site, create a Context named cadl_hard that uses the Advanced Datalayer context reaction (context_advanced_datalayer) to set the site_Name dataLayer tag to the value 'HardCtx'. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A Context 'cadl_hard' exists whose reactions.context_advanced_datalayer.site_Name = 'HardCtx'. E.g. Context::create(['name'=>'cadl_hard','label'=>'...'])->save(); then $c->addReaction(['id'=>'context_advanced_datalayer','site_Name'=>'HardCtx'])->save().
